title: Onprem observability ingest and retention sprint brief
content:
Purpose
This is a short sprint brief and working notes for on-prem observability ingestion and retention changes. Focus: make Prometheus/Grafana metric ingest and OTEL/log shipping resilient in private deployments while reducing cold storage costs and simplifying onprem Terraform module surface. Not a final design — intentionally granular so SREs and infra engs can copy-paste and iterate.

Context and goals
- Current problems: unbounded log spikes blow S3 budgets; Prometheus remote_write bursts sometimes time out under network congestion; OTEL collector configs diverge across customer bundles.
- Sprint goals (2 weeks):
  1) Stabilize remote_write retry/backoff and traffic shaping for Prometheus agents.
  2) Implement two-tier log retention (hot 14d, warm 90d) with optional cold-to-archive policy.
  3) Introduce a minimal "observability_ingest" Terraform module interface so customers can opt into managed ingest routing.
  4) Add evacuation/runbook for archive backend unavailability.

Constraints and non-goals
- Not changing core storage platform (we'll still use object storage compatible APIs for cold).
- Not replacing customer-side agents unless clearly lower risk.

Design notes: metrics ingest
- Prometheus local agent config recommendations (for node-level agent):
  - scrape_interval: 15s default (allow overrides per workload)
  - remote_write: queue_config with max_samples_per_send: 10000, max_shards: 4
  - remote_write retry with exponential backoff: (initial 500ms, max 60s, max_retries: 20)
  - outgoing bandwidth shaping via token_bucket config to limit sustained remote write throughput (recommended burst 10MB/s, sustained 2MB/s for small clusters)
- Consider using Cortex/Thanos write buffers for larger customers. For onprem single-tenant installs, we recommend local Cortex indexer with remote write forwarding.

Design notes: logs/OTEL ingest
- Use OTEL collector as the canonical agent on hosts where customers want full traces + logs. Fallback for lightweight installs: Vector as log-only if they prefer Rust agent.
- Collector pipeline: receiver -> transforms (add tenancy metadata, redact) -> batching -> exporter(s).
- Batching/exporter policies: set sending_batch_size: 2000 events or 5s flush, whichever first.
- Backpressure: configure memory_limiter_processor with memory_limit_mib: 1024, memory_spike_limit_mib: 256.

Retention and tiering
- Hot tier (hot bucket): object storage prefix: s3://redwood-obs/<customer>/hot/ — retention default 14 days, higher IOPS, used for fast logs/alerts.
- Warm tier: s3://redwood-obs/<customer>/warm/ — 90 days, lifecycle transition from hot -> warm at day 14. Warm is lower IOPS and cheaper.
- Cold archive: optional glacier-style prefix s3://redwood-obs/<customer>/archive/ — for >90 days, retrieval has multi-hour latency.
- Migration policy: lifecycle rules applied via Terraform-managed bucket lifecycle.
- Cost guardrails: daily cost alert if hot-tier ingestion > X GB (placeholder: 20GB/day/customer).

Terraform module sketch (observability_ingest)
- Goals: single module to wire up collectors, S3 lifecycle, remote_write targets and IAM bindings. Keep outputs minimal.
- API (variables):
  - name (string) - customer id
  - prometheus_remote_write_endpoints (list of strings)
  - log_sink_backend (string) - values: s3|gcs|minio
  - hot_retention_days (number) - default 14
  - warm_retention_days (number) - default 90
  - collector_mode (string) - values: otel|vector|none
  - enable_evacuate_playbook (bool) - default true
  - tags (map) - optional metadata
- Outputs:
  - s3_bucket_name
  - recorder_endpoint_url
  - collector_config_map_ref

Terraform implementation notes (opinions):
- Do not bake agent configs into module; instead produce a configmap/template and let k8s manifests or customer RPM pick it up. This reduces churn when we tweak policies.
- Put lifecycle rules in a separate sub-module so we can swap storage backends without reapplying agent changes.
- Use versioned module with changelog. Breaking changes require migration guide.

Upgrade plan (high-level steps)
1) Week 0: branch and prototype module. Owner: Marco. Create PR in terraform-modules. (early tests against dev minio)
2) Week 1: unit smoke tests + integration test harness (local minio + small Cortex). Owner: Leah.
3) Week 2: canary on 2 existing onprem customers (low traffic). Roll forward only if no cost regressions or ingestion drops. Owner: Ethan.
4) Week 3: increase canary to 20% of onprem fleet. Monitor queue length, exporter error rates, SLOs.
5) Week 4: full rollout with automated rollback on threshold breaches (see rollback criteria). Owner: Sofia.

Canary & rollout monitoring knobs
- Metric groups to watch: remote_write_queued_samples_total, otel_exporter_failed_spans_total, s3_put_errors, agent_memory_usage_bytes, hot_bucket_size_bytes_per_day.
- SLOs/thresholds for rollback:
  - exporter error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m -> pause rollout
  - agent memory > 80% of configured memory limiter for 5m -> investigate and revert
  - hot tier daily bytes > 150% of baseline for 24h -> pause and revert unless intentional test

Evacuation / archive backend outage runbook (short)
- Detection: S3 5xx increase, put_errors spike, archived retrieval latency > 2h.
- Immediate: enable short-term retention extension on hot to 30 days (Terraform toggle), route new logs to local temporary disk + sidecar forwarder (vector) with local ring buffer.
- Next: trigger replication to alternate bucket/region (preconfigured in module as secondary_backend).
- Postmortem: capture root cause, update module lifecycle rules to add additional preflight checks.

Smoke tests and verification (copyable commands)
- Prometheus remote_write sanity: curl -X POST -d @sample-scrape.json <remote_write_endpoint>/api/v1/write - check metrics about queued samples.
- OTEL collector: run collector with test generator: OTEL_BATCHER_TEST=true ./otelcol --config=collector-test.yaml and assert exporter sends 1000 events in under 30s.
- Log shipping: run vector locally, produce 50MB burst and verify lifecycle transition triggered after retention TTL.

Open questions / risks
- How do we standardize cost thresholds per customer? Need product guidance.
- Some customers have regulatory needs preventing cross-region replication. Module needs a conditional flag to disable secondary backend.
- Do we enforce agent mode (OTEL vs Vector) via module, or leave as advisory? My bias: advisory + supplied config templates so low-friction.

Action items (short)
- Marco: create terraform module repo draft (due 2025-11-12).
- Leah: build integration harness and docs for running local minio + Cortex (due 2025-11-18).
- Ethan: craft canary plan and monitoring dashboards (due 2025-11-22).
- Sofia: write roll-forward and rollback checklist for runbook (due 2025-11-25).

Notes to self / TODOs
- Add example configmap templates for otel collector and vector (with placeholders for redaction rules).
- Draft cost-guard alert thresholds with finance.
- Coordinate with product on default retention numbers for enterprise customers.

References
- Minimal workable OTEL collector pipeline example (in repo): infra/observability/collector-templates/otel-minimal.yaml
- TF module reference: github.com/redwood/terraform-modules/tree/main/observability_ingest (WIP)

End of brief — this should be usable as a sprint kickoff doc. Iterate in-place as we test and discover edge cases.
